name: Unicervical Bicornuate Uterus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: American Society for Reproductive Medicine (ASRM) Classification of Müllerian Anomalies

criteria.description: Presence of a deep external fundal cleft (>10 mm) separating two uterine horns
Single cervical canal despite bicornuate uterine morphology
Confirmation of uterine morphology by MRI or 3D ultrasound
No internal uterine septum present differentiating from septate uterus

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a deep external fundal cleft separating two uterine horns with a single cervical canal confirmed by imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Differentiation from septate and didelphys uterus is critical for management

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bicornuate uterine morphology with single cervix
pathognomonic.notes: Identified on imaging or surgical inspection
searchTerms: uterus with two horns and one cervix
double uterine cavity with single cervix
bicornuate uterus shape with single opening

pathognomonic.notes: Common presenting symptom in affected women

common.symptomName: Dysmenorrhea due to abnormal uterine contractility
searchTerms: painful menstrual cramps from abnormal uterus contractions
dysmenorrhea due to uterine muscle issues
menstrual pain caused by uterine problems

common.notes: Increased risk due to abnormal uterine shape
May include spotting or irregular cycles

occasional.notes: Less frequent than first trimester loss
May be due to uterine structural abnormalities
searchTerms: pelvic pain not linked to periods
chronic pelvic pain unrelated to cycle

rare.notes: May occur if non-communicating horn present
searchTerms: endometriosis caused by blocked uterine horn
growth of uterine lining outside normal location due to obstruction
uterine tissue outside uterus from horn blockage

imaging: MRI showing bicornuate uterus with single endometrial stripe and single cervical canal
3D transvaginal ultrasound demonstrating external fundal cleft >10 mm
Hysterosalpingography showing single cervical canal with two endometrial cavities
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; considered a congenital Müllerian duct anomaly
other: Surgical findings during laparoscopy or laparotomy confirming uterine morphology

distinguishingFeatures: Internal uterine septum with normal external uterine contour
Two endometrial cavities separated by thin fibrous or muscular septum
Usually single external uterine fundal contour
Two separate uterine horns each with its own cervix
Complete duplication of uterine horns and cervices

redFlags: Preterm labor with abnormal uterine shape
references: American Society for Reproductive Medicine. The ESHRE/ESGE consensus on the classification of female genital tract congenital anomalies. Hum Reprod. 2013.
Rock JA, Zacur HA. Müllerian anomalies and their management. Fertil Steril. 2011.
